Ultrasound shows a well-circumscribed solid lesion without suspicious features, which supports a benign process. The biopsy/histology describing a rounded contour with overgrowth of fibrous and glandular tissue fits the biphasic proliferation seen in fibroadenoma. Phyllodes tumor is an important differential (stromal overgrowth, leaf‑like architecture, often more rapid growth and may be larger), but the clinical stability, size, and histologic description favor fibroadenoma over phyllodes or malignancy. Pregnancy-related hormonal stimulation commonly causes or enlarges fibroadenomas, which also matches this patient at 17 weeks gestation.

DIAGNOSIS: Fibroadenoma of the right breast
